files.lesson.md: --- order: 1 unit: parallel node: AC9M7M04 n1 assumes: [AC9M6M04 n1, AC9M6M04 n2] title: Angles at parallel lines summary: "A line crossing two parallel lines makes eight angles. Pairs in the same place at each crossing are corresponding; between the lines on opposite sides, alternate; between the lines on the same side, co-interior." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "Railway tracks, the lines on a car park, the rungs of a ladder: parallel lines crossed by another line. The angles they make come in pairs." app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8169 url: http://127.0.0.1:8169/index.html readySelector: ".pangles" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: lines.yml#explain-pic, caption: "$c$ and $f$ are alternate angles: between the parallel lines, on opposite sides of the crossing line. Both are $60^\\circ$." } explainClip: query: { code: "@lines.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "The angle pairs at parallel lines" say: "A line crossing two parallel lines makes eight angles, in pairs." clip: - caption: { text: "Corresponding: c and g, the same place at each crossing.", say: "Corresponding angles are in the same place at each crossing." } - click: "Angle c, 60°" - click: "Angle g, 60°" - wait: 800 - caption: { text: "Alternate: c and f, between the lines, on opposite sides.", say: "Alternate angles are between the lines, on opposite sides." } - click: "Angle g, 60°" - click: "Angle f, 60°" - wait: 800 - caption: { text: "Co-interior: c and e, between the lines, on the same side.", say: "Co-interior angles are between the lines, on the same side." } - click: "Angle f, 60°" - click: "Angle e, 120°" - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "co-interior" } - wait: 1200 --- Two lines are **parallel** when they go the same way and never meet, like railway tracks. Arrows (>>) on the lines mark them as parallel. A third line that crosses them is a **transversal**. The crossings make eight angles, named $a$ to $h$ here. The angles come in pairs with names, and once you know them you can spot the pairs in any diagram. ## Predict: turning the crossing line ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to what happens to a and e (the same place at each crossing) as the line turns tests whether they see the two crossings as copies of each other." check: type: predict q: "$a$ is above the top line, on the left of the crossing line. $e$ is in the same place at the bottom crossing. If you turn the crossing line, what happens to $a$ and $e$?" options: - "They stay the same size as each other" - "One grows while the other shrinks" - "Nothing links them: they change separately" actual: "They stay the same size as each other. The parallel lines cross the transversal the same way, so the bottom crossing is a copy of the top one, slid along. a and e are corresponding angles." ``` Picture the two crossings. Is one a copy of the other? ## Run: turn the crossing line ```step stage: run insight: "Turning the transversal with a and e picked shows that the same place at each crossing gives the same size, whatever the angle." try: { playground: board, starter: "lines.yml#run", height: 560 } check: { type: board, text: "$a$ and $e$ are picked. Turn the crossing line ($t$) to $120^\\circ$ and watch both. Was your prediction right?", when: "t = 120 and r = 1" } ``` $t$ is the angle the crossing line makes with the parallel lines. Turn it both ways. You can pick other angles too: click them, or use the letters. ## Investigate: the three pairs ```step stage: investigate insight: "Corresponding (same place), alternate (between, opposite sides) and co-interior (between, same side) each take one angle from each crossing. Mia's mistake names a pair at one crossing, which is vertically opposite." try: { playground: board, starter: "lines.yml#pick-a", height: 560 } tasks: - starter: "lines.yml#pick-a" hint: ["Alternate angles are between the parallel lines.", "One on each side of the crossing line: c and f, or d and e."] check: { type: board, text: "This board does not name the pairs. Pick two alternate angles.", when: "r = 2", explain: "c and f, or d and e: between the lines, on opposite sides of the crossing line." } - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#mia" text: "Mia names a pair of angles. Click the line where her reasoning goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: vertically-opposite-pair explain: "Line 3: b and c are at the same crossing, opposite each other, so they are vertically opposite. Alternate angles are one at each crossing, between the parallel lines. (Vertically opposite angles are equal too, so line 4's b = c is true, for a different reason.)" - picture: { ref: lines.yml#letters, caption: "Two parallel lines crossed by a transversal, with the angles $a$ to $h$." } check: type: question q: "Which pair is co-interior?" options: ["$c$ and $e$", "$c$ and $f$", "$c$ and $g$", "$b$ and $c$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Those are on opposite sides: alternate.", "Those are in the same place at each crossing: corresponding.", "Those are at one crossing: vertically opposite."] explain: "c and e are both between the lines and both on the left of the crossing line: co-interior." ``` ### Pick a pair Here are the pairs. Each takes one angle from each crossing. ```worked \text{corresponding: } a \text{ and } e :: The same place at each crossing: both above their line, on the left. (An F shape.) \text{alternate: } c \text{ and } f :: Between the parallel lines, on opposite sides of the crossing line. (A Z shape.) \text{co-interior: } c \text{ and } e :: Between the parallel lines, on the same side. (A C shape.) \text{vertically opposite: } b \text{ and } c :: At one crossing, opposite each other. Not a parallel-lines pair: both are at the same crossing. ``` Then pick two alternate angles on the board. ### Find the mistake Read Mia's reasoning one line at a time. Where are b and c? ### Co-interior ## Modify: one change at a time ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: the crossing line leaning the other way (corresponding, co-interior, then vertically opposite to keep it apart), lines that are not parallel, then the edge case of a right angle." try: { playground: board, starter: "lines.yml#pick-b", height: 560 } tasks: - starter: "lines.yml#pick-b" hint: "The same place at each crossing: above the line and left, at the top and at the bottom." check: { type: board, text: "The crossing line leans the other way now. Pick two corresponding angles.", when: "r = 1", explain: "a and e, b and f, c and g, or d and h." } - starter: "lines.yml#pick-b" hint: "Between the lines, on the same side of the crossing line." check: { type: board, text: "Pick two co-interior angles.", when: "r = 3", explain: "c and e, or d and f." } - starter: "lines.yml#pick-b" hint: "Both at one crossing, opposite each other." check: { type: board, text: "Pick two vertically opposite angles.", when: "r = 4", explain: "a and d, b and c, e and h, or f and g: at one crossing, opposite each other." } - starter: "lines.yml#tilt" hint: "Move w back to 0, then away again. Watch c and f." check: type: question q: "The lower line is tilted by $w$, so the lines are not parallel. Are $c$ and $f$ still alternate angles?" options: ["Yes: they are in alternate places, but they need not be equal", "No: alternate angles need parallel lines", "Yes, and they are still equal"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The name is about where the angles are. What parallel lines add is that they are equal.", "Look at the sizes: with w = 15°, c is 60° and f is 45°."] explain: "The names say where the angles are. Only when the lines are parallel are alternate (and corresponding) angles equal, and co-interior angles add to 180°." - starter: "lines.yml#turn" hint: "What angle does a crossing line make when it is square to the lines?" check: { type: board, text: "Edge case: turn the crossing line until all eight angles are the same size.", when: "t = 90", explain: "At t = 90° the crossing line is perpendicular to the parallel lines: all eight angles are right angles." } ``` ### Corresponding Each task changes one thing. This board does not name the pairs, so the check tells you. ### Co-interior ### Vertically opposite ### Not parallel ### A right angle ## Practise: name the pair ```step stage: practise insight: "Naming pairs from a fixed diagram, mixed, with vertically opposite as the planted mix-up; the review keeps angles on a straight line fresh." tasks: - picture: { ref: lines.yml#letters, caption: "The angles $a$ to $h$." } check: type: question q: "$d$ and $e$ are" options: ["alternate", "corresponding", "co-interior", "vertically opposite"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Are they in the same place at each crossing?", "Are they on the same side of the crossing line?", "They are at different crossings."] explain: "Between the lines, on opposite sides: alternate." smaller: check: type: question q: "Look at $d$ and $e$. Are they at the same crossing, or one at each?" options: ["One at each crossing", "Both at the same crossing"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "d is at the top crossing and e is at the bottom one."] explain: "d is at the top crossing and e at the bottom. So they can't be vertically opposite. Next, check which side of the crossing line each one is on." - picture: { ref: lines.yml#letters, caption: "The angles $a$ to $h$." } check: type: question q: "$b$ and $f$ are" options: ["corresponding", "alternate", "co-interior", "vertically opposite"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "b is above the top line, not between the lines.", "b is above the top line, not between the lines.", "They are at different crossings."] explain: "Both above their line, on the right: the same place at each crossing, so corresponding." - picture: { ref: lines.yml#letters, caption: "The angles $a$ to $h$." } check: type: question q: "$a$ and $d$ are" options: ["vertically opposite", "alternate", "corresponding", "co-interior"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Both are at the top crossing.", "Both are at the top crossing.", "Both are at the top crossing."] explain: "At one crossing, opposite each other: vertically opposite." - check: type: answer q: "Review: $a$ and $b$ are on a straight line. $a = 115^\\circ$. What is $b$?" answer: "65" feedback: - ["115", "a and b are not equal: they make a straight line together."] - ["245", "Angles on a straight line add to 180°, not 360°."] explain: "Angles on a straight line add to 180°: 180 − 115 = 65°." ``` ### Name it Use the picture: same place, between and opposite, between and same side, or one crossing? ### Name it again ### One crossing ### Review: a straight line ## Make: a pair that adds to 180° ```step stage: make insight: "Finding a pair between the lines that adds to 180° reverses the lesson: from what the angles do back to where they are." try: { playground: board, starter: "lines.yml#make", height: 560 } hint: ["Look only between the parallel lines: c, d, e and f.", "Which two of those add to 180°? Check with the sizes."] check: { type: board, text: "Pick two angles between the parallel lines, at different crossings, that add to $180^\\circ$.", when: "u >= 3 and u <= 4 and v >= 5 and v <= 6 and s = 180", explain: "c and e, or d and f: co-interior angles. (At t = 90° the alternate pairs c and f, d and e add to 180° too, but co-interior pairs always do.)" } ``` Find a pair, then turn the crossing line. Do they still add to $180^\circ$? Stretch: which pairs add to $180^\circ$ but are not between the lines? ## Make: are they parallel, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "The rule runs both ways: parallel lines have equal corresponding angles, so unequal corresponding angles mean the lines are not parallel." hint: ["Are the two angles in the same place at each crossing?", "What would be true of them if the lines were parallel?"] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "Two lines are crossed by a transversal. Angle a, above the top line on the left, is 72°. The angle in the same place at the bottom crossing is 75°. Are the lines parallel? On paper, give your reasons." steps: - ["The two angles are in the same place at each crossing, so they are corresponding", "same place, one at each crossing"] - ["If the lines were parallel, corresponding angles would be equal", "that is the rule for parallel lines"] - ["72° and 75° are not equal, so the lines are not parallel", "they would have to match"] picks: - step: 3 q: "Why are the lines not parallel?" options: - "The corresponding angles are not equal, and they would be if the lines were parallel" - "75° is bigger than 72°, and bigger angles mean parallel lines" - "Any two lines crossed by a transversal are parallel" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Which is bigger does not matter. Parallel lines need the two angles equal.", "Only some lines are parallel. The angles tell you which."] criteria: - "I named the pair as corresponding." - "I said what parallel lines would do to that pair." - "I compared 72° and 75° and gave my answer." explain: "Corresponding angles are equal when the lines are parallel. These are 72° and 75°, so the lines are not parallel." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The angles are made up for the task, and real measurements are never exact. Sketch it, write the three steps, then choose the reason. ```teacher summary: Students turn a transversal across two parallel lines, see that the same place at each crossing gives the same angle, and learn to name corresponding, alternate and co-interior pairs in any orientation, keeping them apart from vertically opposite angles (AC9M7M04, node 1). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 10 min goals: - I can find corresponding, alternate and co-interior angles where a line crosses two parallel lines. - I can tell these pairs apart from vertically opposite angles. - I can explain that the names say where the angles are, and parallel lines make the pairs equal or add to 180°. struggle: Seeing which angles match. Ask students to shade the angles they think equal the marked one, then turn the line and see which stay equal. before: > Do the Run board and the Investigate board yourself first. Students need angles on a straight line and vertically opposite angles (Year 6). The one idea: each pair takes one angle from each crossing, and the name says where they are (same place; between and opposite sides; between and same side). The common mistake is naming a pair at one crossing (vertically opposite) as alternate; it is planted after the names, in Mia's reasoning. The boards in Investigate, Modify and Make do not name the pairs: students pick, and the check says whether the pair is right. F, Z and C shapes are given as memory aids only; the Modify board leans the other way so students do not rely on them. running: - "Predict: take a show of hands. Students who chose 'one grows, the other shrinks' may be thinking of a and b (a straight line)." - "Run: ask students to say why the bottom crossing looks like the top one (the lines go the same way)." - "Investigate: draw the eight angles on the board and colour each pair as you name it. Ask: does each pair use both crossings?" - "Modify: before the tilt task, ask what changes if the lines are not parallel. Let the board show it." - "Make: collect the pairs students found and ask why only the pairs between the lines always work." - "Make on paper: ask what the corresponding angles would be if the lines were parallel." stuck: - see: A student names b and c as alternate (Mia's mistake). ask: Which crossing is each angle at? fix: The parallel-line pairs take one angle from each crossing. b and c are vertically opposite. - see: A student mixes up alternate and co-interior. ask: Are both angles on the same side of the crossing line? fix: "Same side: co-interior (C). Opposite sides: alternate (Z)." - see: A student cannot find pairs when the diagram is turned. ask: Where are the parallel lines? Which angles are between them? fix: Shade the band between the parallel lines first; alternate and co-interior angles are inside it. stretch: "Draw a diagram with three parallel lines and one transversal. How many corresponding pairs are there? (Each of the 4 positions gives a pair for each two of the three lines (top and middle, middle and bottom, top and bottom): 4 × 3 = 12 pairs.)" support: "Use the board with names on (the Run board): pick pairs and read the names before trying the boards without them." leads: > Next: finding angles with parallel lines (node 2), which adds the rules: corresponding and alternate equal, co-interior add to 180°. Where it leads: angle sums of triangles and polygons (the next unit), and geometric reasoning with reasons in Years 8 to 10. exit: q: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. Which angle pairs are equal, and which pair adds to 180°? a: Corresponding angles and alternate angles are equal (so are vertically opposite angles); co-interior angles add to 180°. explain: > A line crossing two **parallel** lines (a **transversal**) makes eight angles, $a$ to $h$. Each pair below takes one angle from each crossing: - **corresponding**: the same place at each crossing, such as $a$ and $e$ (an F shape); - **alternate**: between the parallel lines, on opposite sides of the transversal, such as $c$ and $f$ (a Z shape); - **co-interior**: between the parallel lines, on the same side, such as $c$ and $e$ (a C shape). Two angles at one crossing, opposite each other, are **vertically opposite**: not one of these pairs. ```

# Mia's reasoning for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: mia
Mia looks at angles b and c.
b and c are on opposite sides of the crossing line.
So b and c are alternate angles.
Alternate angles are equal, so b = c.
# endregion
